statement.p: (b) Find the best linear approximation of g(x,y) for (x,y) near (2,1).
(c) Use the approximation in part (b) to estimate g(1.99, 1.03).

static.solution:
(a) We have g_x = \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+y+11}}, \quad \hbox{ so } g_x(2, 1) = \frac{1}{2} and g_y = \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x^{2}+y+11}}, \quad \hbox{ so } g_y(2, 1) = \frac{1}{8}. Thus \nabla g(2,1) = \frac{1}{2}\, \vec i + \frac{1}{8}\, \vec j.
(b) Using the value g(2, 1) = 4 and the partial derivatives in part (a) we have g(x, y) = \sqrt{x^{2}+y+11} \approx 4 + \frac{1}{2} (x-2) + \frac{1}{8} (y-1).
(c) Using the linearization in part (b), we have g(1.99, 1.03) \approx 4 + \frac{1}{2} (2 - 1.99) + \frac{1}{8} (1 - 1.03) = 3.99875.
